sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。
现在是凌晨五点二十五分。

sentences.en: outside of the City Hall in Peter Merrittsburg, South Africa.
sentences.zh: 在南非彼得马里茨堡的市政厅外。

sentences.en: And Shahida Tungo is ready to go on a run.
sentences.zh: 沙希达·通戈正准备去跑步。

sentences.en: She's wearing a white running skirt and knee socks, one pink, one blue, and she's cracking jokes.
sentences.zh: 她穿着一件白色的跑步短裙和及膝袜，一只粉色，一只蓝色，她还在开玩笑。

sentences.en: Listen, I'm not there to run for the money, so I have to look good.
sentences.zh: 听着，我来可不是为了赚钱跑的，所以我得让自己看起来很好看。

sentences.en: I can't be fast, so I must be cute.
sentences.zh: 我跑不快，所以我必须长得可爱。

sentences.en: The road around her is packed with other equally chipper runners, adjusting their race numbers, snapping selfies, and dancing.
sentences.zh: 她周围的路上挤满了同样兴高采烈的跑者，他们正在调整号码布、自拍和跳舞。

sentences.en: Altogether, there are about 13,000 people here, and they're not getting ready for a 5K or a 10K or even a marathon.
sentences.zh: 总共大约有一万三千人来到这里，他们可不是在准备五公里、十公里甚至马拉松。

sentences.en: This is the start line of the Comrades, which is 56 miles long.
sentences.zh: 这是同志超级马拉松的起跑线，全长五十六英里。

sentences.en: That's Ryan Lenora Brown, a reporter in South Africa who was there the morning of the race in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 那是瑞安·勒诺拉·布朗，一位南非记者，今年八月比赛当天的早晨她就在现场。

sentences.en: Most years, more than 15,000 people run the Comrades, way more than run any other ultramarathon in the world.
sentences.zh: 大多数年份里，有超过一万五千人参加同志马拉松，远远超过世界上任何其他超级马拉松。

sentences.en: For reference, about 25,000 people ran the last Boston Marathon, but the Comrades is more than twice as long.
sentences.zh: 作为参考，大约有两万五千人跑了去年的波士顿马拉松，但同志马拉松的长度是它的两倍多。

sentences.en: And as a foreigner in South Africa, I've been haunted for a long time by a question.
sentences.zh: 作为南非的一个外国人，长期以来我一直被一个问题困扰。

sentences.en: Why the hell do South Africans think running a race like this for fun is a normal thing to do?
sentences.zh: 南非人到底凭什么觉得为了好玩而跑这样一场比赛是一件很正常的事？

sentences.en: Not only is it very, very long, the Comrades goes to a part of South Africa whose name sounds pretty ominous when you're doing two back-to-back marathons through it.
sentences.zh: 不仅比赛非常非常长，同志马拉松还要穿过南非的一个地方，当你连续跑两个马拉松穿过它时，这个名字听起来很不吉利。

sentences.en: The Valley of a Thousand Hills.

sentences.zh: 好孩子没什么可抱怨的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure, but I'm here now.
sentences.zh: 我不确定，但我现在在这儿。

sentences.en: Shahida is one of the Comrades' pacers, who are appointed by the race to help groups of runners trying to finish in a certain time.
sentences.zh: 沙希达是同志马拉松的官方配速员之一，由赛事指派来帮助试图在特定时间内完赛的跑者群体。

sentences.en: In South Africa, these pacers are called bus drivers, and the people they pace are their bus.
sentences.zh: 在南非，这些配速员被称为公交司机，他们带领的人群被称为公交车。

sentences.en: Shahida paces the Comrades' slowest bus, made up of runners trying to finish just before the race's 12-hour cutoff.
sentences.zh: 沙希达带的是同志马拉松最慢的一组，由那些试图在比赛十二小时关门前惊险完赛的跑者组成。

sentences.en: She's a kind of evangelist for running very slowly, very far.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是跑得很慢、跑得很远的布道者。

sentences.en: I just want to make the slower runners like myself believe that the how is irrelevant, whether you're crawling or rolling or whatever, as long as you're going forward at Comrades,
sentences.zh: 我只是想让像我一样慢的跑者相信，怎么跑并不重要，不管你是爬着、滚着还是别的什么，只要你在同志马拉松上前进，

sentences.en: Today, she's got a little piece of paper tucked into her pocket, telling her what times and distances she needs to hit to come in just under that 12-hour mark.
sentences.zh: 今天，她的口袋里塞着一张小纸条，上面写着她需要达到什么时间和距离，才能刚好在十二小时大关之前冲线。

sentences.en: Basically, she's aiming to do this like a human metronome.
sentences.zh: 基本上，她的目标就像一个人类节拍器一样运作。
全天保持十三分钟一英里的配速。

sentences.en: No faster, and definitely no slower.
sentences.zh: 不能更快，也绝对不能更慢。

sentences.en: Over the course of the day, they'll follow a route that weaves through what feels like all of South Africa.
sentences.zh: 在这一天的时间里，他们将沿着一条路线穿行，感觉就像走遍了整个南非。

sentences.en: The race winds through wealthy suburbs full of cafes and craft breweries, and sleepy, run-down little farming towns.
sentences.zh: 比赛穿过富裕的郊区，那里到处都是咖啡馆和精酿啤酒厂，还有沉睡、破败的小农镇。

sentences.en: It cuts across the sugarcane plantations that first brought British colonizers to this region in the 1800s.
sentences.zh: 它横穿甘蔗种植园，正是这些种植园在十九世纪将英国殖民者带到了这个地区。

sentences.en: There are shack settlements and rich private schools.
sentences.zh: 这里有棚户区，也有贵族私立学校。

sentences.en: A few minutes after I see Shahida, they play the national anthem.
sentences.zh: 我看到沙希达几分钟后，国歌响起了。

sentences.en: And then another song comes on.
sentences.zh: 接着另一首歌放了出来。

sentences.en: It's a haunting tune that migrant laborers used to sing on their long journeys home from South Africa's gold mines.
sentences.zh: 这是一首凄美的曲调，曾经是契约劳工在从南非金矿回家的漫长旅程中哼唱的。

sentences.en: They were underground, and it was dark.
sentences.zh: 他们曾在地下，里面一片漆黑。

sentences.en: It's a very draining task to do, and that's exactly what comrades is.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常消耗精力的任务，而这正是同志马拉松的意义所在。

sentences.en: You know, you're going to trot along the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你要一路小跑完成全程。

sentences.en: So it is just saying, I can do it.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是在说，我能做到。

sentences.en: I will keep going, and no matter how hard it is, I have a purpose why I'm doing this.
sentences.zh: 我会坚持下去，不管有多难，我做这件事都有我的目的。

sentences.en: And then the cannon goes off.
We start the watch, and we're off.
Around the world, ultramarathons are having a moment.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，超级马拉松正迎来高光时刻。

sentences.en: These are races that are any distance longer than a standard 26.2-mile marathon.
sentences.zh: 这些都是任何长于标准二十六点二英里马拉松的比赛。

sentences.en: The number of people running them more than quadrupled between 2010 and 2020.
sentences.zh: 从二零一零年到二零二零年，参加这类比赛的人数翻了四倍多。

sentences.en: There are now thousands of these races annually.
sentences.zh: 如今每年都有数千场这样的比赛。

sentences.en: But in most of the world, ultras are pretty niche, and they attract a very particular demographic.
sentences.zh: 但在世界大部分地区，超马还很小众，它们吸引着非常特定的群体。

sentences.en: Your average ultrarunner in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国或欧洲，你的平均超级马拉松跑者

sentences.en: or Europe is a well-educated married man about 45 years old.
sentences.zh: 是一个受过良好教育、已婚的约四十五岁男子。

sentences.en: In other words, they look a lot like me.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们看起来很像我。

sentences.en: And you only have to eyeball the start line of an ultramarathon in North America or Europe
sentences.zh: 你只需看一眼北美或欧洲超级马拉松的起跑线

sentences.en: to see that this is still an overwhelmingly white sport.
sentences.zh: 就会发现这仍然是一项压倒性白人的运动。

sentences.en: But in South Africa, it's a different story.
sentences.zh: 但在南非，情况则完全不同。

sentences.en: So all kinds of people run comrades.
sentences.zh: 所以各种各样的人都会跑同志马拉松。

sentences.en: White, black, Indian, colored, male, female, others, wealthy, poor.
sentences.zh: 白人、黑人、印度人、有色人种、男性、女性、其他人、富人、穷人。

sentences.en: If you live in South Africa, you definitely know someone who runs ultras.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在南非，你肯定认识跑超马的人。

sentences.en: Here, ultramarathons are the stuff of a whole country's New Year's resolutions and midlife crises.
sentences.zh: 在这里，超级马拉松是一个国家的新年愿望和中年危机。

sentences.en: They're the kind of thing that a totally ordinary, not-athletic person wakes up one day and decides they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是一个完全普通、毫无运动细胞的人某天醒来决定要去做的事。

sentences.en: It might be your doctor, your kid's teacher, the man pumping your gas, the woman who cleans your house.
sentences.zh: 那可能是你的医生、你孩子的老师、给你加满油的男士、给你家打扫卫生的女士。

sentences.en: In one of the most economically unequal countries in the world,
sentences.zh: 在世界上经济最不平等的国家之一，

sentences.en: extreme distance running is a sport that feels like it includes everybody.
sentences.zh: 极限长跑是一项让人觉得包容所有人的运动。

sentences.en: And, improbably, that inclusiveness happened during one of the darkest, most divided moments in South Africa's history,
sentences.zh: 而出人意料的是，这种包容性发生在南非历史上最黑暗、分裂最严重的时期之一，

sentences.en: during the final years of apartheid.
sentences.zh: 也就是种族隔离的最后几年。

sentences.en: When the Comrades Ultramarathon first started,
sentences.zh: 当同志超级马拉松刚开始的时候，

sentences.en: it wasn't the little Rainbow Nation and Nikes that it later became.
sentences.zh: 它并不是后来那个小彩虹国度和耐克的世界。

sentences.en: In fact, in its earliest days, the Comrades looked a lot like ultramarathons elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在其早期，同志马拉松看起来很像其他地方的超级马拉松。

sentences.en: So back then, look, I mean, this is 1921.
sentences.zh: 所以在当时，听着，我的意思是，这是一九二一年。

sentences.en: This is South Africa in its early days.

sentences.zh: 这是马苏拉尼·马马博洛。

sentences.en: He's a South African sports journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一名南非体育记者。

sentences.en: And also, like so many of his countrymen, a Comrades runner.
sentences.zh: 同时，和他的许多同胞一样，他也是一名同志马拉松跑者。

sentences.en: The race was only open to white people.
sentences.zh: 这项比赛只对白人开放。

sentences.en: It was just the white people who ran, and only men, actually.
sentences.zh: 只有白人跑步，而且实际上只限男性。

sentences.en: The Comrades was started by a white South African World War I veteran named Vic Clapham.
sentences.zh: 同志马拉松是由一名叫维克·克拉普哈姆的南非白人一战老兵发起的。

sentences.en: To honor his Comrades who had fallen in the war,
sentences.zh: 为了纪念他在战争中牺牲的战友，

sentences.en: he designed to run between his hometown of Pietermaritzburg
sentences.zh: 他设计了一条路线，连接他的家乡彼得马里茨堡

sentences.en: and the coastal city of Durban, about 56 miles away.
sentences.zh: 和大约五十六英里外的沿海城市德班。

sentences.en: And a few people apparently signed up.
I think there was about 34 people who signed up to run the race.
sentences.zh: 我想当时大约有三十四人报名参加比赛。

sentences.en: And it was a big deal because, I mean, who runs from Maritzburg to Durban?
sentences.zh: 这可是件大事，因为我的意思是，谁会从马里茨堡跑到德班？

sentences.en: The race alternated directions each year.
sentences.zh: 比赛每年往返交替方向。

sentences.en: And in those early days, the press called it a, quote,
sentences.zh: 而在早期，媒体称之为，引述，
小伙子们穿着橄榄球靴跑步。

sentences.en: They stopped for a beer and curried chicken at a hotel along the way.
sentences.zh: 他们在沿途的一家酒店停下来喝啤酒、吃咖喱鸡。

sentences.en: This definitely wasn't the first ultra-marathon in the world.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是世界上第一场超级马拉松。

sentences.en: Actually, even long before the first modern marathon was held in the 1896 Olympics,
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至早在十八九六年奥运会举办第一场现代马拉松很久以前，

sentences.en: a form of super long-distance racing had been popular in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 一种超长距离赛跑在美国和欧洲就已经很流行了。
在其鼎盛时期，即十九世纪七八十年代，这是一项极受欢迎的观众运动，

sentences.en: And in its heyday, in the 1870s and 80s, it was a hugely popular spectator sport
sentences.zh: 参赛者竞走距离长达一千五百英里。

sentences.en: where competitors race-walked distances up to 1,500 miles.
sentences.zh: 这项运动如此受欢迎，以至于最大牌的选手能赚到相当于数百万美元的奖金。

sentences.en: The sport was so popular that the biggest names earned the equivalent of millions of dollars of prize money.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，同志马拉松则是一场更具业余性质的比赛。

sentences.en: The Comrades, on the other hand, was a much more amateur affair.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，比赛规模有所增长，但并不戏剧性。

sentences.en: Over the decades, the race grew in size, but not dramatically.
sentences.zh: 到了二十世纪六十年代，每年大概有一百五十个小伙子在跑。

sentences.en: By the 1960s, there were maybe 150 guys running it every year.

sentences.zh: 偶尔会有女性或有色人种出现在起跑线上，

sentences.en: Every once in a while, a woman or a person of color would show up on the start line
sentences.zh: 没有号码布就非官方地跑完整场比赛。

sentences.en: and run the race unofficially, without a number.
sentences.zh: 组织者通常不会把他们拉出赛道，

sentences.en: The organizers generally didn't pull them off the course,
sentences.zh: 但他们的名字从未被记录在官方完赛名单中。

sentences.en: but they never got recorded in the official finishers liSt.
sentences.zh: 某些年份，组织者甚至阻止他们进入比赛终点的体育场，

sentences.en: In some years, the organizers actually blocked their entry to the stadium where the race ended,
sentences.zh: 所以他们永远无法冲过终点线。

sentences.en: so they would never cross the finish line.
sentences.zh: 除了将百分之九十的人口排除在外之外，

sentences.en: Between excluding 90% of the population from participating,
sentences.zh: 再加上长达五十六英里，

sentences.en: and then also being, you know, 56 miles long,
sentences.zh: 同志马拉松似乎注定要默默无闻。

sentences.en: the Comrades seemed doomed to obscurity.
sentences.zh: 但随后，形势开始发生变化。

sentences.en: But then, the ground started to shift.
sentences.zh: 到二十世纪七十年代，实行种族隔离的南非是非洲仅存的由白人统治的国家之一，

sentences.en: By the 1970s, apartheid South Africa was one of the last white-ruled countries in Africa,
sentences.zh: 它正面临来自全球要求变革的压力。

sentences.en: and it was coming under global pressure to change.
sentences.zh: 反种族隔离运动人士认为，迫使南非妥协的最佳方法之一

sentences.en: Anti-apartheid campaigners believed that one of the best ways to force South Africa's hand
sentences.zh: 就是将其从世界其他地方孤立开来。

sentences.en: would be to isolate it from the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 南非活动人士组织了对该国出口商品的抵制。

sentences.en: South African activists organized boycotts of the country's exports.
sentences.zh: 他们向国际公司施压，要求其撤出对该国的投资，

sentences.en: They pressured international companies to divest from the country,
sentences.zh: 并敦促全世界的艺术家和音乐家不要去那里演出。

sentences.en: and urged the world's artists and musicians not to perform there.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是要求你们做出政治决定。

sentences.en: We are not asking that you make a political decision.
sentences.zh: 我们不是要求你们做出经济决定。

sentences.en: We're not asking you to make an economic decision.
sentences.zh: 德斯蒙德·图图大主教，南非反种族隔离领袖。

sentences.en: Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the South African anti-apartheid leader.
sentences.zh: 我们是要求你们做出道德决定。

sentences.en: We're asking you to make a moral decision.
sentences.zh: 那些在南非投资的人，看在上帝的份上，

sentences.en: Those who invest in South Africa, for goodness sake,
must know that they do so,
and in doing so are upholding and buttressing
sentences.zh: 世界上有史以来最恶劣的系统之一。

sentences.en: one of the most vicious systems the world has ever known.
sentences.zh: 对许多南非人来说，最痛苦的孤立形式之一发生在体育领域。

sentences.en: For many South Africans, one of the most painful forms of isolation came in the realm of sports.
sentences.zh: 到二十世纪七十年代，该国不再被允许参加奥运会或世界杯。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, the country was no longer allowed to compete in the Olympics or the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离政府极力游说国际足联不要把他们开除，

sentences.en: The apartheid government lobbied hard to FIFA to not kick them out,
sentences.zh: 但他们对种族隔离的执念如此诡异，以至于他们提出了一个奇怪的妥协想法：

sentences.en: but they were so bizarrely committed to segregation that they pitched some weird compromise idea
sentences.zh: 在一九六六年世界杯上派出一支全白人球队，

sentences.en: of sending an all-white team to the World Cup in 1966,
sentences.zh: 然后在一九七〇年派出一支全黑人球队。

sentences.en: and then an all-black team in 1970.

sentences.zh: 我认为在我们这样的社会里，你永远不可能有正常的体育，

sentences.en: I don't think you can ever have normal sport in the kind of society we have,
sentences.zh: 一个完全不正常的社会。
活动人士深知这种退出世界体育界的做法

sentences.en: Activists understood how this withdrawal from world sports
sentences.zh: 会使白人政府感到自己犹如社会弃儿。

sentences.en: would make the white government feel like pariahs.

sentences.zh: 南非迫切希望重新回到世界的各项比赛中。

sentences.en: South Africa desperately wanted back into the world's competitions.
sentences.zh: 因此，从二十世纪七十年代初开始，

sentences.en: And so, beginning in the early 1970s,
sentences.zh: 它开始尝试将国内体育赛事一体化。

sentences.en: it began to experiment with integrating domestic sports.
sentences.zh: 它开始尝试将国内体育赛事一体化。

sentences.en: Running was one of the firSt.
sentences.zh: 跑步是其中最早的项目之一。

sentences.en: In 1974, sports journalist Mazzalane Mamabolo's uncle, Titus Mamabolo,
sentences.zh: 1974年，体育记者马扎拉内·马马博洛的叔叔蒂图斯·马马博洛

sentences.en: became the first black athlete to win an integrated national championship in the five kilometers.
sentences.zh: 成为第一位在五公里项目中赢得融合全国锦标赛的黑人运动员。

sentences.en: And suddenly, black South Africa started believing
sentences.zh: 突然之间，南非的黑人群体开始相信

sentences.en: that we can compete with white people and even beat them.
sentences.zh: 我们能够与白人竞争，甚至战胜他们。

sentences.en: And I think because of that, the whole country started shifting towards,
sentences.zh: 我想正因如此，整个国家开始转向

sentences.en: let's open up to the black people.

sentences.zh: “同胞”马拉松的组织者被逼入了绝境。

sentences.en: They didn't want to be left behind.
sentences.zh: 他们不想被时代抛在后面。

sentences.en: the organizers opened up the race to people of color.
sentences.zh: 组织者向有色人种开放了这场比赛。

sentences.en: At the time, distance running was enjoying a worldwide boom in popularity.
sentences.zh: 当时，长跑运动在全世界正迎来一股普及热潮。

sentences.en: It was also beginning to include more and more women.
sentences.zh: 它也开始吸引越来越多的女性参与。

sentences.en: For a long time, the conventional wisdom held that women couldn't run marathons
